::: {#def-boundedness .theorem}
## Boundedness

A component function takes values in a finite set: there is a finite $\mathcal{D}$ such that $g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}) \in \mathcal{D}$ for all $\mathbf{X} \in \{0,1\}^n$. An exposure mapping is bounded if it is [separable](#def-separability) and all its component functions are bounded.

Boundedness is a homogeneity assumption because it is what makes exposure comparable across units: finitely many exposure levels, each occupied by many units, is what allows one function to be estimated from the whole population.
:::
